title: Commissioner of Internal Revenue v. San Roque Power Corporation
summary: The Supreme Court laid down definitive rules on the prescriptive periods for filing judicial claims for VAT refunds. The 120-day period for the CIR to act on the administrative claim is mandatory and jurisdictional, and the 30-day period to appeal to the CTA is also jurisdictional.
doctrine: The 120+30 day periods for VAT refund claims are mandatory and jurisdictional. The taxpayer must wait for the lapse of the 120-day period before filing the judicial claim with the Court of Tax Appeals. Premature filing renders the petition without jurisdiction. The 30-day period to appeal is also jurisdictional.
fullText:
CARPIO, J.:

These consolidated cases present the issue of the proper interpretation of the prescriptive periods for filing judicial claims for refund of excess input VAT.

Section 112(C) of the NIRC provides that the Commissioner shall grant a refund or issue a tax credit certificate within one hundred twenty (120) days from the date of submission of complete documents. In case of full or partial denial, or failure to act within the 120-day period, the taxpayer may appeal to the Court of Tax Appeals within thirty (30) days.

The 120-day period is mandatory and jurisdictional. The taxpayer cannot file the judicial claim before the lapse of the 120-day period, as the CTA has no jurisdiction over premature petitions.
